lesson.title: Ida y Vuelta, Salida & Llegada
lesson.subtitle: Buying one-way (sencillo / de ida) and round-trip (de ida y vuelta) tickets with para + city

hook.title: Decoding Station Boards: Ida y Vuelta, Salida & Llegada
hook.content:
When you look up at the departure board in Atocha Station in Madrid or buy a ticket at the window, three transparent words greet you:
• **un billete de ida** = 'a one-way ticket' (lit. 'of going', from *ir* 'to go'!).
• **un billete de ida y vuelta** = 'a round-trip / return ticket' (lit. 'of going and turning-back', from *volver* 'to return/revolve'!).
• **la salida** = 'the exit / departure' (remember our false friend: *el éxito* is 'success', while **la salida** is the physical exit or departure!).

pattern.title: Ordering Tickets at the Window
pattern.content: *Un billete de ida y vuelta para Toledo, por favor* ('A round-trip ticket to Toledo, please').

exercises.prompt: Match each English expression with its Spanish partner:

matching_pairs.english: a round-trip ticket ('of going and return')
matching_pairs.german: un billete de ida y vuelta

exercises.target_answer: un billete de ida y vuelta, un billete de ida, para Madrid, para mañana, la salida
exercises.meaning: a round-trip ticket ('of going and return'), a one-way ticket ('of going'), for / to Madrid (destination arrow), for tomorrow (deadline/target date), the exit / the departure (not éxito!)
exercises.explanation: ida comes from ir ('to go'); vuelta comes from volver ('to turn/return'); la salida is the exit or departure.

exercises.prompt: At the airport or train station, you see a sign that says 'SALIDA'. What does it mean (and how does it contrast with 'éxito')?
exercises.explanation: From salir ('to go out / depart'), la salida means both 'the physical exit' and 'departure time'!

exercises.target_answer: Dos billetes para Madrid, por favor
exercises.explanation: Dos billetes + para Madrid, por favor.

exercises.idea: say that tomorrow you are going to Madrid by train ('en tren')
cues: Tomorrow I am going → Mañana voy
idea_parts: Tomorrow I am going to Madrid → Mañana voy a Madrid
exercises.target_answer: Mañana voy a Madrid en tren
exercises.meaning: Tomorrow I am going to Madrid by train
exercises.explanation: Mañana voy a Madrid en tren — Spanish uses en + vehicle (en tren, en coche, en autobús) for 'by train / by car'!

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: Quiero dos billetes para mañana por favor
exercises.target_answer: Quiero dos billetes para mañana por favor
exercises.meaning: I want two tickets for tomorrow, please
cues: for tomorrow, please: para mañana, por favor
exercises.explanation: Quiero dos billetes para mañana, por favor.

summary.outcome: Buy tickets, travel by train (en tren), and distinguish la salida ('exit/departure') from el éxito ('success').

use_example.german: Quiero dos billetes para Madrid mañana en tren, por favor.
use_example.english: I want two tickets for Madrid tomorrow by train, please.

summary.takeaway: Travel by a vehicle takes en without an article: en tren ('by train').
summary.curiosity_teaser: Next branch ([5141] Familia, Profesiones & Pasiones): learn why Spanish drops 'un/una' before professions!

twist.prompt: Assemble: 'I am going to the station today'

billete.etymology_derivation: un billete de ida y vuelta = 'a round-trip ticket'.

tren.context_phrase: Tomo el tren a las ocho.
tren.context_translation: I take the train at eight.

estación.etymology_derivation: Covers both 'train station' and 'season of the year'.

ir.context_translation: I am going to go tomorrow.
ir.etymology_derivation: Latin īre ('to go', preserved in English exit 'go out' and transit 'go across')!

voy.context_translation: I am going to visit Madrid.
voy.etymology_derivation: Followed by a + infinitive, voy a expresses the near future.

para.english_meaning: for (recipient, destination, deadline), in order to
para.etymology_derivation: Old Spanish pora (por + a) — think of para as a forward arrow pointing at the recipient, destination, deadline, or goal ('in order to').

mañana.context_translation: Tomorrow I am going to work.
mañana.etymology_derivation: As an adverb (mañana) it means 'tomorrow'; as a feminine noun (la mañana) it means 'the morning' (mañana por la mañana = 'tomorrow morning')!

hoy.etymology_derivation: Latin hodiē lost its middle d and became hoy (the exact cousin of the -hui in French aujourd'hui!).
